Latitudinarianism
/ˌlæt.ɪˌtuː.dɪˈnɛər.i.əˌnɪ.zəm/
noun
Latin latitudo — breadth. Historical label for broad-church Anglican temper; now general for doctrinal minimalism that prizes peace by shrinking what is worth contending for.

Biblical Definition

Latitudinarianism is the temperament that prizes breadth and peace by shrinking the load of doctrines worth contending for. Peace is a fruit of the Spirit; false peace is a snare. Jude says contend for the faith once delivered (Jude 3). Paul anathematizes another gospel (Galatians 1:6–9). John refuses fellowship with anti-Christ denial of the Son (2 John 9–11). Romans 14 liberty is for disputable matters — not for the deity of Christ, the resurrection, or justification by faith. Healthy breadth: charity on millennial charts. Unhealthy breadth: smile while the gospel bleeds out.

What it is: doctrinal minimalism-as-virtue; boundary allergy.
What it is not: patience with weak consciences; not evangelistic wisdom; not refusing needless fights.

Webster 1828 Definition

From latitude/breadth — broadness of interpretation or communion.

Key Scripture

Jude 1:3 — "Contend for the faith once delivered."

Galatians 1:6-9 — "Another gospel — anathema."

2 John 1:9-11 — "No fellowship with denial of the Son."

1 Timothy 4:16 — "Watch life and doctrine."

Romans 14:1-5 — "True adiaphora — disputable matters."

Ephesians 4:14-15 — "Truthing in love."

Modern Corruption

“Doctrine divides” as a creed; orthodoxy treated as unkind.

expand to see more

“Doctrine divides” as a creed; church as brand lounge; orthodoxy treated as unkind. Pair with sectarianism as opposite ditches on the same road. Be hard to offend on preferences. Be impossible to move on the gospel. Breadth with a spine.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Latin latitudo — breadth.

expand to see more

Latin latitudo — breadth. The question is never “breadth or not?” but “breadth of what — and at what cost to the faith once delivered?”

Usage

""Latitudinarianism shrinks the load of doctrines worth contending for until the gospel bleeds out.""

""Romans 14 is for disputable matters — not the deity of Christ.""

""Breadth with a spine: hard to offend on preferences, impossible to move on the gospel.""
